policy: A record is a person the text names or a person it speaks of. The woman who had an issue of blood twelve years is spoken of in three places and named in none; Jesus says Daughter to her, which is how he addresses her and not what she is called. She stays one record, headed by what the text says of her, and the three words in which he addresses her are hers.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's ruling of 2026-09-30 that Daughter is no name, each word read against its verse by an agent

says.name: Woman with an issue of blood
says.distinguisher: who touched the hem of Jesus' garment (MAT 9:20-22)
says.notes: Jesus addresses her as 'Daughter' (MAT 9:22; MRK 5:34; LUK 8:48); the text does not give her name.

rulings.why: 'Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole': the word is said to the woman who came behind him and touched the hem of his garment (9:20), diseased with an issue of blood twelve years.
'And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace': said to the woman who had had an issue of blood twelve years and touched his garment (5:25-29).

'And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace': said to the woman having an issue of blood twelve years who touched the border of his garment (8:43-44).
